notes.content: DIVERSITY REQUIREMENT FOR CAL STATE LA GRADUATION

The articulation information in Assist.org not only shows a link to the admission requirements (aka our Major Specific Criteria webpage) but also Cal State LA graduation requirements that may be completed at the lower-division level, prior to transferring to the University. The diversity requirement is a graduation requirement , not an admission requirement. The diversity requirement may be completed prior to, or after, transferring to the University. For the Cal State LA degree, students will be required to complete two courses (six units) certified as diversity courses, at least one focusing on issues of race and ethnicity and their intersectionality with other social categories that structure inequality in society. These courses can be completed either at the lower-division or upper-division level from among courses satisfying GE requirements. Please view the General Education agreements on Assist.org for the lower-division courses that will meet the Diversity (d) and Race & Ethnicity (re) Requirements.

notes.content: Overview The objective of the Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science is to prepare qualified students for careers involving the design of computer systems and their applications to science and industry. The program provides an excellent foundation in all core areas of computer science with the opportunity to choose electives in a variety of specialized fields. Requirements for the Major The total number of units required for the Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science is 120 units, of which 94 units are in the major. Computer Science students are required to take 43 units of General Education (GE) of which 21 units are met by courses in the major. Consult with an advisor in the department for the specific number of units required in all areas of the degree, including GE and free electives.
notes.contentHtml:
Overview


The objective of the Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science is to prepare qualified students for careers involving the design of computer systems and their applications to science and industry. The program provides an excellent foundation in all core areas of computer science with the opportunity to choose electives in a variety of specialized fields.  


Requirements for the Major


  • The total number of units required for the Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science is 120 units, of which 94 units are in the major. 
  • Computer Science students are required to take 43 units of General Education (GE) of which 21 units are met by courses in the major.


Consult with an advisor in the department for the specific number of units required in all areas of the degree, including GE and free electives.
